nodes.name: Tverberg number $T(d,r)$
nodes.statement: $T(d,r)=(d+1)(r-1)+1$, the smallest $n$ such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits an $r$-partition with a common point in the convex hulls.

nodes.name: Tverberg-Reay number $T(d,r,k)$
nodes.statement: Smallest positive integer $n$ such that for any list $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ there is an $r$-partition $N_1,\ldots,N_r$ with every $k$ of the $r$ convex hulls $\mathrm{conv}\, a(N_j)$ having a point in common.

nodes.name: Positive basis $P=\{p_0,\ldots,p_d\}$
nodes.statement: Vertices of a $d$-simplex centered at the origin: $\sum_{i=0}^d p_i=\underline{0}$ and each $d$ of them are linearly independent. Define rays $R_i=\{\lambda p_i:\lambda>0\}$.

nodes.name: Non-negative representation and support
nodes.statement: The unique representation $x=\sum \xi_i p_i$ with $\min \xi_i = 0$. The support is $\mathrm{supp}\, x = \{i\in D : \xi_i>0\}$.

nodes.name: Index set $I(C)$ and ray union $R(I)$
nodes.statement: For $C\subseteq X$, $I(C)=\{i\in D:C\cap R_i\neq\emptyset\}$. For $I\subseteq D$, $R(I)=\cup\{R_i:i\in I\}$.

nodes.name: Lower / higher on a ray
nodes.statement: For $a=\alpha p_i, b=\beta p_i\in R_i$ with $\alpha,\beta>0$, $a$ is lower than $b$ on $R_i$ iff $\alpha<\beta$ (equivalently $\|a\|<\|b\|$).

nodes.name: Highest, middle, lowest points $p_{i,1},p_{i,2},p_{i,3}$
nodes.statement: On each ray $R_i$ the three points of $X$ are denoted $p_{i,1}$ (highest), $p_{i,2}$ (middle), $p_{i,3}$ (lowest).

nodes.name: $(M,X)$-selection
nodes.statement: For $M\subset D$, an $(M,X)$-selection $S$ is a subset of $X$ of size $|M|$ consisting of exactly one point on each ray $R_j,\, j\in M$.

nodes.name: General position of $X$
nodes.statement: $X$ is in general position if for every $M\subset D$ with $2\le|M|=m\le d$ and every $\bar m$ pairwise disjoint $(M,X)$-selections $S_1,\ldots,S_{\bar m}$, $\cap_i \mathrm{aff}\, S_i$ is a single point if $\bar m=m$ and empty if $\bar m>m$.

nodes.name: Common rays $I(J)$
nodes.statement: For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, $I(J)=\bigcap_{j\in J} I(C_j)$. A ray $R_i$ is common (for the collection $\{C_j\}_{j\in J}$) iff $i\in I(J)$.

nodes.name: Weight function $W$
nodes.statement: For $k$ distinct parts $C_{j_1},\ldots,C_{j_k}$ and ray $R_i$: $W(\cdot,R_i)=0$ if $R_i\cap C_{j_s}=\emptyset$ for some $s$; otherwise $W=1+\#\{s:|C_{j_s}\cap R_i|>1\}$.

nodes.name: Bad / good partition
nodes.statement: An $r$-partition is bad if some two parts have disjoint convex hulls; it is good if every two parts' convex hulls have a point in common.

nodes.name: Separating hyperplane $H_{k,\ell}$
nodes.statement: $H_{k,\ell}=\mathrm{aff}(R_k\cup R_\ell)$; $H_{k,\ell}(j)$ is the closed half-space bounded by $H_{k,\ell}$ that contains $R_j$.

nodes.name: Tverberg's Theorem
nodes.statement: If $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $n>(d+1)(r-1)$, then $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ can be partitioned into $r$ disjoint parts $N_1,\ldots,N_r$ whose convex hulls $\mathrm{conv}\{a_i:i\in N_j\}$ have a point in common.

nodes.name: Radon's Theorem
nodes.statement: Any set of $d+2$ or more points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be partitioned into two disjoint parts whose convex hulls meet.

nodes.name: Helly's Theorem (used)
nodes.statement: If $r>d+1$ and every $d+1$ of the convex hulls $\mathrm{conv}\, a(N_j)$ meet, then they all meet; consequently $T(d,r,k)=T(d,r)$ for $d+1\le k\le r$.
assumptions: every $d+1$ of $\{\mathrm{conv}\, a(N_j)\}_{j=1}^r$ have a common point

nodes.name: Reay's Conjecture
nodes.statement: $T(d,r,k)=T(d,r)$ for all $2\le k\le r$.

nodes.name: Main Theorem (Reay's conjecture for $k\ge\lfloor(d+3)/2\rfloor$)
nodes.statement: For every $d\ge 2$ and $r\ge\lfloor (d+3)/2\rfloor$: $T(d,r,\lfloor (d+3)/2\rfloor)=T(d,r)=(d+1)(r-1)+1$.

nodes.name: Second Theorem (Reay's conjecture for $d<rk/(r-k)-1$)
nodes.statement: For every $2\le k<r$ and dimension $d<\frac{kr}{r-k}-1$: $T(d,r,k)=T(d,r)=(d+1)(r-1)+1$.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of non-negative representation
nodes.statement: Every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ has a unique representation $x=\xi_0 p_0+\cdots+\xi_d p_d$ with $\min\{\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_d\}=0$.

nodes.name: Support containment
nodes.statement: If $C\subseteq X$ and $x\in\mathrm{conv}\, C$, then $\mathrm{supp}\, x\subseteq I(C)$.

nodes.name: Restriction to common rays
nodes.statement: Suppose $C\subseteq X$ and $x\in\mathrm{conv}\, C$. If $I(C)\neq D$, then $x\in\mathrm{conv}(C\cap R(\mathrm{supp}\, x))$.

nodes.name: Disjointness via lower/higher on rays
nodes.statement: Let $I\subsetneq D$ and $C,C'\subset R(I)$ finite. If for each $i\in I$ every point of $C\cap R_i$ is lower than every point of $C'\cap R_i$, then $\mathrm{conv}\, C\cap \mathrm{conv}\, C'=\emptyset$.
assumptions: for each $i\in I$, every point of $C\cap R_i$ is lower than every point of $C'\cap R_i$

nodes.name: Empty intersection criterion (key technical proposition)
nodes.statement:
Suppose $U\subsetneq D$, $C_1,\ldots,C_n\subset X$ ($n\ge2$), with (1) $ igcap_{
u=1}^n I(C_
u)\subseteq U$, (2) $I(C_
u)\subsetneq D$ for $
u=1,2$, (3) on each $i\in U$ every point of $C_1\cap R_i$ is lower than every point of $C_2\cap R_i$. Then $ igcap_{
u=1}^n \mathrm{conv}\, C_
u=\emptyset$.
assumptions: for each $i\in U$, every point of $C_1\cap R_i$ is lower than every point of $C_2\cap R_i$

nodes.name: Bound on $|I(C_1)\cap I(C_2)\setminus U|$
nodes.section: 2.2 Completion of the proof of Theorem $T(d,r,\lfloor(d+3)/2\rfloor)$
nodes.statement: Under the notations of Section 2.2, $|I(C_1)\cap I(C_2)\setminus U|\le \lfloor (d-1)/2\rfloor$.
assumptions: notation as in Section 2.2 (orderings of $C_1,C_2$, $U=U_1$ or $U_2$ chosen as the larger)

nodes.name: Perturbation preserves badness
nodes.statement: If $X=C_0\cup C_1\cup C_2\cup C_3$ is a bad 4-partition of $X$, it remains bad after a sufficiently small perturbation of $X$.
conclusions: $\exists\delta>0$ such that any perturbation of size $<\delta$ leaves the partition bad

nodes.name: Small $|I(C_i)|$ forces bad partition
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}=(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)$ be a 4-partition of $X$. If $|I(C_i)|<3$ for some $i$, then $\mathcal{C}$ is bad.

nodes.name: Two-side lower implies disjoint hulls
nodes.statement: Suppose $I(C_i)=\{j,k,\ell\}$, $I(C_j)=\{i,k,\ell\}$. If $C_i$ is lower than $C_j$ on both $R_k$ and $R_\ell$, then $\mathrm{conv}\, C_i\cap\mathrm{conv}\, C_j=\emptyset$.
assumptions: $C_i$ is lower than $C_j$ on both $R_k$ and $R_\ell$

nodes.name: Lowest/middle/highest distribution
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{C}=(C_0,C_1,C_2,C_3)$ is a good partition (with $|C_i|=3$), then each $C_i$ contains exactly one lowest, one middle and one highest point.
conclusions: each $C_i$ contains exactly one $p_{\cdot,1}$, one $p_{\cdot,2}$, one $p_{\cdot,3}$

nodes.name: Common rays govern intersections of convex hulls
nodes.statement: For $J\subset\{1,\ldots,r\}$, if $I(C_j)\subsetneq D$ for every $j\in J$, then $\bigcap_{j\in J}\mathrm{conv}\, C_j=\bigcap_{j\in J}\mathrm{conv}(C_j\cap R(I(J)))$.

nodes.name: Mutual rays bound — base case
nodes.statement: Given $\{C_j\}_{j\in J}$ with $|J|=k$: if $|I(J)|=m<k$ and each common ray contains exactly one point of each $C_j$, then $\bigcap_{j\in J}\mathrm{conv}\, C_j=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Generalized mutual rays bound ($m<k-t$)
nodes.statement: With $\{C_j\}_{j\in J}$, $|J|=k$, $|I(J)|=m$, and $t$ the number of $C_j$ that contain more than one point on at least one common ray: $m<k-t$ implies $\bigcap_{j\in J}\mathrm{conv}\, C_j=\emptyset$.
assumptions: $t$ parts have $|C_j\cap R_i|>1$ for some $i\in I(J)$

nodes.name: Characterization of good $(5,3,2)$-partitions
nodes.statement: A partition $(C_1,C_2,C_3)$ of $X$ (with $d=5,r=3$) is good iff for every $1\le i<j\le 3$ there exists exactly one ray on which $C_i$ is lower than $C_j$ and exactly one on which $C_j$ is lower than $C_i$.
assumptions: $X$ as constructed (12 points on 6 rays, 2 per ray, in general position)
conclusions: $(C_1,C_2,C_3)$ is good iff for every pair $\{i,j\}$ there is exactly one ray with $C_i$ lower than $C_j$ and exactly one with $C_j$ lower than $C_i$

nodes.name: Hyperplane separating $C_1$ from $C_2$ in the (5,3,2) construction
nodes.statement: For positive $a,b,c,d$ with $a+b=c+d$, the hyperplane $H=\{a\xi_i+b\xi_j=c\xi_k+d\xi_\ell\}$ weakly separates $C_1$ from $C_2$, with $C_1\cap H=C_1\cap (R_m\cup R_n)$ and $C_2\cap H=C_2\cap(R_m\cup R_n)$.

nodes.name: Perturbation that separates $\mathrm{conv}\, C_1$ from $\mathrm{conv}\, C_2$
nodes.statement: If $\max\{u_i,u_j\}>\min\{u_k,u_\ell\}$ and $p\in C_1\cap(R_m\cup R_n)$, then $p\rightsquigarrow p'=p+\varepsilon\vec u$ (small $\varepsilon>0$) separates $\mathrm{conv}\, C_1$ from $\mathrm{conv}\, C_2$.
conclusions: replacing $p$ by $p'=p+\varepsilon\vec u$ yields $\mathrm{conv}\, C_1'\cap\mathrm{conv}\, C_2=\emptyset$

nodes.name: Equality case $d+1=rk/(r-k)$
nodes.statement: When $d+1=rk/(r-k)$, equivalently $k\binom{r}{k}=(d+1)\binom{r-1}{k}$: if every $k$ of the $\mathrm{conv}\, C_j$ have a point in common, then each ray $R_i$ carries $r-1$ points of $X$ in $r-1$ different parts, and any $k$ convex hulls intersect in a single point — providing the basis for a perturbation argument (used for $d=5,r=3,k=2$).

nodes.name: Hyperplane stability across the three perturbations
nodes.statement: Since the third-step direction $\vec u''=(1,0,0,0,1,0)$ is fixed in advance, only finitely many separating hyperplanes can arise; choosing $\varepsilon,\varepsilon'$ small enough keeps $p_{0,1}$ and $p_{0,1}'$ (and possibly $p_{5,1},p_{5,1}'$) on the same side of each.

nodes.name: Non-negative representation
nodes.statement: $x=\xi_0 p_0+\xi_1 p_1+\cdots+\xi_d p_d$, where $\min\{\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_d\}=0$.

nodes.name: Lower bound: $\sum_i W\ge k$
nodes.statement: If $\bigcap_{s=1}^k \mathrm{conv}\, C_{j_s}\neq\emptyset$, then $\sum_{i=0}^d W((C_{j_1},\ldots,C_{j_k}),R_i)\ge k$.

nodes.name: Upper bound: $\sum_J W\le\binom{r-1}{k}$
nodes.statement: For each $i\in D$: $\sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k\le r}W((C_{j_1},\ldots,C_{j_k}),R_i)\le\binom{r-1}{k}$.

nodes.name: Combined bound on $k\binom{r}{k}$
nodes.statement: $k\binom{r}{k}\le\sum_J\sum_i W\le(d+1)\binom{r-1}{k}$, equivalent to $d\ge\frac{rk}{r-k}-1$.

nodes.name: Compute $T(d,r,k)$ (Reay's question)
nodes.statement: Determine the smallest $n$ such that every $n$-point set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits an $r$-partition in which every $k$ of the convex hulls of parts have a common point.

nodes.name: Disprove Reay's conjecture for some triple $(d,r,k)$
nodes.statement: For some $r,k$ with $2\le k<r$ and $d$ large enough, does $T(d,r,k)<T(d,r)$ hold? In particular: is $T(d,3,2)<2d+3$ from some $d$ on (perhaps already $d\ge 6$)?

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (uniqueness of non-negative representation)
nodes.statement: Use that $P$ spans $\mathbb{R}^d$ linearly with the only dependency $\sum \lambda p_i=0$, and pick $\lambda=\min\alpha_i$ to zero out a coefficient.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (restriction to common rays)
nodes.statement:
Write $x=\sum\gamma_
u c_
u$ with $c_
u\in C$; rays appearing in $C$ contribute positive coefficients to the non-negative representation, hence those indices lie in $\mathrm{supp}\, x$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (disjointness via lower/higher)
nodes.statement: Pick points $s_i$ on each $R_i$ between $C\cap R_i$ and $C'\cap R_i$; their affine hull is a hyperplane separating $C$ from $C'$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition $\ref{prop:C1..Cn}$ (key empty intersection criterion)
nodes.statement: Assume $x\in\bigcap \mathrm{conv}\, C_\nu$, derive $\mathrm{supp}\, x\subseteq U$, restrict to common rays, then apply Proposition $\ref{prop:ClowerThanC'}$ to obtain a contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of bound on $|I(C_1)\cap I(C_2)\setminus U|$
nodes.section: 2.2 Completion of the proof of Theorem $T(d,r,\lfloor(d+3)/2\rfloor)$
nodes.statement: Algebraic manipulation of $|I(C_1)\cap I(C_2)|$, $|S_1\cap S_2|$, $|M_1\cap S_2|$ using inequalities (\ref{equ:Ci>I(Ci)+Mi}), (\ref{eq:ineq}), (\ref{equ:|C2|<|I(C1)|}).

nodes.name: Proof of Main Theorem
nodes.section: 2.2 Completion of the proof of Theorem $T(d,r,\lfloor(d+3)/2\rfloor)$
nodes.statement: Construct $X$ as $r-1$ points on each of $d+1$ rays; for any $r$-partition pick $C_1,C_2$ minimizing certain counts, choose $U$, attach $C(i)$ for the leftover indices, then apply Proposition $\ref{prop:C1..Cn}$ to conclude $\bigcap\mathrm{conv}=\emptyset$ for $n\le\lfloor (d+3)/2\rfloor$ parts.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem $T(3,4,2)=13$
nodes.statement: Catalogue all 18 good 4-partitions of the 12-point set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, then perturb $p_{0,1}$ and $p_{3,3}$ in two steps to convert every good partition into a bad one while preserving badness elsewhere.

nodes.name: Proof of Second Theorem
nodes.statement: Induction on $r$ with base $r=2$ trivial; for $r>2$ use the induction hypothesis when some $C_r$ visits all rays, otherwise combine the lower bound (Proposition $\ref{prop:m<k-t}$) and the upper bound (weight-rebalancing) to obtain $k\binom{r}{k}\le(d+1)\binom{r-1}{k}$, equivalent to $d\ge\frac{rk}{r-k}-1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem $T(5,3,2)=13$
nodes.statement: Use Remark $\ref{rmk:d+1=rk/(r-k)}$ to characterize the 120 good partitions; apply Proposition $\ref{prop:U_that_separates_c1_from_c2}$ three times with directions $\vec u=(0,1,2,3,4,5)$, $\vec u'=(5,4,3,2,1,0)$, $\vec u''=(1,0,0,0,1,0)$ to spoil all 120 in three perturbation steps.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (small $|I(C_i)|$)
nodes.statement: Case analysis on $|I(C_0)|\in\{1,2\}$; in each case either some other part misses $R_0\cup R_1$ entirely (apply Prop $\ref{prop:supp_x}$) or apply Prop $\ref{prop:C1..Cn}$ with $U=\{0\}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (lowest/middle/highest distribution)
nodes.statement: If two lowest points lie in $C_i$, by Prop $\ref{prop:CiLowerThanCj}$ the partition is bad. Symmetric for highest. So the four lowest distribute one-per-part and likewise for highest; the middles must distribute by counting.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (perturbation preserves badness)
nodes.statement: Choose $\delta>0$ smaller than half of the minimum convex-hull distance. Any perturbation by $<\delta$ moves convex combinations by $<\delta$, so disjoint hulls remain disjoint.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (common rays govern intersection)
nodes.statement: Apply Prop $\ref{prop:supp_x}$ to obtain $\mathrm{supp}\, x\subseteq I(J)$, then Prop $\ref{prop:CcapR(supp_x)}$ to land $x$ inside $\mathrm{conv}(C_j\cap R(I(J)))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (mutual rays bound — base case)
nodes.statement: Each $C_j\cap R(I(J))$ is $m$ linearly independent points spanning a hyperplane in the $m$-dim space; intersecting $k>m$ such hyperplanes is empty by general position.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition $m<k-t$
nodes.statement: Split $J=S\sqcup T$ where $S$ contains parts meeting each common ray exactly once. Then $|S|=k-t>m$, and the affine intersection of $|S|$ hyperplanes in an $m$-space is empty.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (good partition characterization for $(5,3,2)$)
nodes.statement: By Remark $\ref{rmk:d+1=rk/(r-k)}$, each pair of parts shares exactly two common rays; by Proposition $\ref{prop:C1..Cn}$ with $n=2$, $C_i$ must be lower than $C_j$ on one and higher on the other.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (perturbation separates $\mathrm{conv}\, C_1,\mathrm{conv}\, C_2$)
nodes.statement: Choose $a=d=\delta,\,b=c=2\Delta$, apply Prop $\ref{prop:A_separate_hyperline}$ to obtain a separating hyperplane $H$, then push $p$ across $H$ via $\varepsilon\vec u$ to strictly separate the simplices.

nodes.name: Canonical $(d+1)\cdot(r-1)$ ray construction
nodes.statement: $d+1$ rays $R_0,\ldots,R_d$ emanating from the origin, positively spanning $\mathbb{R}^d$ (vertices of a centered simplex), with $r-1$ points chosen on each ray. $|X|=(d+1)(r-1)=T(d,r)-1$.

nodes.name: Three good $(3,4)$-partitions with prescribed top-of-$R_0$ assignment
nodes.statement: Three good $4$-partitions of the 12-point set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ with $p_{0,1}\in C_1$, $p_{0,2}\in C_2$, $p_{0,3}\in C_3$ (Figure $\ref{fig:partitionsOf4RaysInto4Parts}$); the remaining 15 are obtained by permuting $\{1,2,3\}$.

nodes.name: Yellow-blue-red $(5,3)$-partition
nodes.statement: A model good $3$-partition of the 12-point set in $\mathbb{R}^5$: each color (red/yellow/blue) occupies one of three positions on each of the 6 rays, drawn schematically; all 120 good partitions are obtained by permuting $R_1,\ldots,R_5$.

nodes.name: 20 exceptional good $(5,3)$-partitions
nodes.statement: The 20 good partitions on which the first perturbation $\vec u=(0,1,2,3,4,5)$ fails to separate the red and yellow simplices, namely those with $\max\{i,j\}<\min\{k,\ell\}$ in (\ref{equ:RaysOfC1_C2_C3}).

nodes.name: Setup: the example set $X$
nodes.statement: Construct $X$ as $r-1$ chosen points on each of the rays $R_0,\ldots,R_d$; $|X|=(d+1)(r-1)=T(d,r)-1$.

nodes.name: Order parts so $|C_1|$ and $|C_2\cap R(I(C_1))|$ are minimal
nodes.statement: Reorder $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ so $|C_1|\le|C_i|$ ($i\ge 2$) and $|C_2\cap R(I(C_1))|\le|C_i\cap R(I(C_1))|$ ($i\ge 3$). Deduce $|I(C_1)|\le|C_1|\le d$ and $|I(C_2)|\le d$.

nodes.name: Decompose $I(C_i)=S_i\sqcup M_i$ and define $U$
nodes.statement: Split $I(C_i)$ into singletons $S_i$ and multi-occurrence indices $M_i$. Split $S_1\cap S_2$ by which of $C_1,C_2$ is lower into $U_1,U_2$ and let $U$ be the larger of the two.

nodes.name: Bound $|I(C_1)\cap I(C_2)\setminus U|\le \lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor$
nodes.statement: Apply the inequality $|I(C_1)\cap I(C_2)\setminus U|\le\lfloor (d-1)/2\rfloor$ proved in Proposition $\ref{prop:|I(C_1)cap I(C_2)setminus U|}$.

nodes.name: Choose $C(i)$ avoiding $R_i$ for each leftover $i$
nodes.statement: For each $i\in I(C_1)\cap I(C_2)\setminus U$ pick $C(i)\in\{C_3,\ldots,C_r\}$ with $C(i)\cap R_i=\emptyset$; possible because $|(X\setminus(C_1\cup C_2))\cap R_i|\le r-3$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition $\ref{prop:C1..Cn}$ and conclude
nodes.statement: The collection $\{C_1,C_2\}\cup\{C(i)\}$ has size $n\le 2+\lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor=\lfloor(d+3)/2\rfloor$ and satisfies the hypotheses; hence $\mathrm{conv}\, C_1\cap\mathrm{conv}\, C_2\cap\bigcap_i\mathrm{conv}\, C(i)=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Reduce to 18 good partitions
nodes.statement: Argue that all good 4-partitions have $|C_i|=|I(C_i)|=3$; then enumerate the 18 good partitions via Propositions $\ref{prop:CiLowerThanCj},\ref{prop:LowestMiddleHighest}$.

nodes.name: Step 1: replace $p_{0,1}\to p'_{0,1}$
nodes.statement: Set $p'_{0,1}=p_{0,1}+\delta' p_{3,1}$ with small $\delta'>0$. This separates $\mathrm{conv}\, C_1'\cap\mathrm{conv}\, C_3'=\emptyset$ when $p_{0,1}\in C_1$ (similarly for $C_2$).

nodes.name: Identify remaining good partitions via $p_{3,3}$ position
nodes.statement: If $p_{0,1}\in C_3$ then $p_{0,2}\in C_i$ ($i\in\{1,2\}$) forces $p_{3,3}\in C_i$ via Proposition $\ref{prop:LowestMiddleHighest}$.

nodes.name: Step 2: replace $p_{3,3}\to p''_{3,3}$
nodes.statement: Set $p''_{3,3}=p_{3,3}+\delta'' p_{0,3}$. Since $C_1\subset H_{2,3}(0)$, $C_0\subset H_{2,3}(1)$, this pushes $p_{3,3}$ strictly into $\mathrm{int}\, H_{2,3}(0)$ and yields $\mathrm{conv}\, C_1''\cap\mathrm{conv}\, C_0''=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Conclude $T(3,4,2)=13$
nodes.statement: After Steps 1 and 2, $X''$ is a 12-point set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ where every 4-partition has two parts with disjoint convex hulls.

nodes.name: Base case $r=2$
nodes.statement: For $r=2$ the assertion is vacuous.

nodes.name: Inductive reduction when some $C_r$ hits every ray
nodes.statement: If some part $C_r$ has $I(C_r)=D$, delete it and apply the induction hypothesis on $\tilde X=X\setminus C_r$, using $\frac{rk}{r-k}-1<\frac{(r-1)k}{r-1-k}-1$.

nodes.name: Handle the case $k=r-1$ via supports
nodes.statement: If $k=r-1$, $\bigcap I(C_j)=\emptyset$ implies $\mathrm{supp}\, x=\emptyset$, hence $x=\underline{0}$, contradiction.

nodes.name: Lower bound (\ref{eq:buba})
nodes.statement: From Proposition $\ref{prop:m<k-t}$ derive $\sum_i W((C_{j_1},\ldots,C_{j_k}),R_i)\ge k$ whenever $\bigcap\mathrm{conv}\, C_{j_s}\neq\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Upper bound (\ref{eq:baba}) via weight rebalancing
nodes.statement: Show $W(R_i)$ is maximized when each ray's $r-1$ points lie in distinct parts; in that case $W(R_i)=\binom{r-1}{k}$, hence $\sum_J W\le\binom{r-1}{k}$.

nodes.name: Combine and derive $d\ge\frac{rk}{r-k}-1$
nodes.statement: Combining (\ref{eq:buba}) and (\ref{eq:baba}) gives $k\binom{r}{k}\le(d+1)\binom{r-1}{k}$, equivalent to $d\ge\frac{rk}{r-k}-1$, contradicting $d<\frac{rk}{r-k}-1$.

nodes.name: Reduce to 120 good partitions
nodes.statement: Use Remark $\ref{rmk:d+1=rk/(r-k)}$ (since $d+1=6=rk/(r-k)$) and Prop $\ref{prop:goodPartitions532}$ to enumerate the $120=5!$ good 3-partitions.

nodes.name: First perturbation: $p_{0,1}\to p_{0,1}+\varepsilon(0,1,2,3,4,5)$
nodes.statement: Apply Prop $\ref{prop:U_that_separates_c1_from_c2}$ with $\vec u=(0,1,2,3,4,5)$, $C_1$=red, $C_2$=yellow, $m=0$. Separates 100 of the 120 good partitions; 20 fail (those with $\max\{i,j\}<\min\{k,\ell\}$).

nodes.name: Second perturbation: $p_{5,1}\to p_{5,1}+\varepsilon'(5,4,3,2,1,0)$
nodes.statement: Apply Prop $\ref{prop:U_that_separates_c1_from_c2}$ with $\vec u'=(5,4,3,2,1,0)$, $m=5$, separating blue from yellow. Resolves 14 of the remaining 16 cases; fails only on the two subcases of (1) where $p_{5,1}$ is blue.

nodes.name: Third perturbation: $p_{2,1}\to p_{2,1}+\varepsilon''(1,0,0,0,1,0)$
nodes.statement: Apply Prop $\ref{prop:U_that_separates_c1_from_c2}$ with $\vec u''=(1,0,0,0,1,0)$, $m=2$, separating blue from red on the remaining 6 cases.

nodes.name: Conclude $T(5,3,2)=13$
nodes.statement: After three perturbations, every 3-partition of the resulting 12-point set in $\mathbb{R}^5$ has two parts with disjoint convex hulls, so $T(5,3,2)\ge 13=T(5,3)$, hence equality.
